name: bench-cobol
title: archived .cbl/.CBL files: COBOL programs and copybooks, synthetic stubs, comic-book lists
labels: an LLM judge (Claude Sonnet 4.6), else the study's rules
sampling: population-sampled with weights (uniform by-file sample; synthetic stubs drawn down to 40)
source: Software Heritage, via PL-ultimate-llm's COBOL study (swh-evidence-v1@274fa4cc8)
strengths: drawn uniformly from the archive's 276,831 .cbl/.CBL files, with population weights
real COBOL as archived: Japanese comments in Shift-JIS, copybooks, generated code, both casings
contamination as the archive has it: 41 % of the files are synthetic stubs
weaknesses: labels by one LLM judge, or by the study's rules where the judge's gate skipped the file
files the rules call `other` (foreign code, metadata) are left out: no label
the file name alone scores 91 % unweighted
the rules and the cascade's candidates were built from these files
